_comment: Reorders Italian lessons at index 10-17 (it-food, it-possession, it-transport, it-requests, it-reflexive, it-past, it-plans, it-days) into the six-archetype variety plan in scripts/content/lessons/ITALIAN-VARIETY.md (rotation B E D A C F B E). For each lesson `steps` and `legacyExercises` are reordered together so the practice step whose activityId is a legacy exercise id stays at the same index as that exercise; the top-level `activities` array, all ids, `completionPolicy`, `entryStepId` and every other field are untouched. The information intro stays first and its `purpose` stays notice; graded steps stay practice; the two real `transfer` steps (it-food, it-requests) are carried through unchanged. Archetypes B-F name seven practice slots and do not name `review`, so `review` is placed immediately before the final listening step (the position archetype A gives it), matching the French payload's convention. Applied by scripts/content/differentiate-first-words.py; do not edit courses/ by hand.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which Italian word means “I take / I will have”?
legacyExercises.explanation: Regular -ere verbs commonly use -o for io and -i for tu: prendere → prendo, prendi. In a café, prendo un caffè can mean I will have a coffee. Keep the accents on caffè and tè. Acqua is feminine: un’acqua.

legacyExercises.prompt: Which Italian word means “my (feminine singular)”?

legacyExercises.prompt: Which Italian word means “I get up”?
legacyExercises.explanation: Reflexive verbs use a pronoun referring back to the subject. Alzarsi means to get up: io mi alzo, tu ti alzi. Mi and ti go before the finite verb. Alle sette means at seven o’clock; alle combines a + le.
